title: Git Tips
content:
GitHub workflows

Depending on how you deliver, test and maintain you code there are different strategies on how to use git. As a general rule thumb integrate as often as possible and have as few branches as possible. Below three different git workflows are described that can be used depending on you prerequisites

The GitHub Flow

Deploy feature branch and merge to main when approved

https://guides.github.com/introduction/flow/

Trunk based development with PRs

Release from main

https://cloud.google.com/solutions/devops/devops-tech-trunk-based-development

The git flow

Develop and master as long lived branches where master represent last release and feature branches are used for developing new features.

https://nvie.com/posts/a-successful-git-branching-model/

Git commands and configuration

Cultivating Git a nice git history

This article describes how to use git for keeping a clean git history

https://megakemp.com/2019/03/20/the-case-for-pull-rebase/

Handling multi platform development

Make sure that diffs work

https://docs.github.com/en/github/using-git/configuring-git-to-handle-line-endings

and some template files

https://github.com/alexkaratarakis/gitattributes

Making your Git Diff more legible

There is a tool called diff-so-fancy that can be used to more clearly highlight the diffs.

It can be found here: https://github.com/so-fancy/diff-so-fancy and works for Windows, Linux and MacOS.
